Pull Request Revisions

RevisionDescription

Refactored Headscale Change Management SystemMajor architectural changes including: - Introduced new change management system with `change.ChangeSet` - Replaced notifier with a more efficient batcher mechanism - Simplified node state tracking and update propagation - Enhanced mapper with builder pattern and improved response generation - Updated state management to use new change propagation model - Improved testing infrastructure and added more robust integration tests
r38
Refactored node update and notification systemMajor architectural changes in Headscale include: 1. Replaced legacy notifier with a new change propagation system 2. Introduced a lock-free batcher for handling node updates 3. Simplified change tracking with a new `ChangeSet` type 4. Removed direct dependency on node notifier in multiple components 5. Enhanced mapper and state management to use new change propagation mechanism 6. Improved error handling and logging in node update workflows 7. Added more robust handling of node lifecycle events 8. Implemented more granular update tracking for nodes and users
r37
Refactored node connection and batching logicSimplified batcher implementation, removed unnecessary transaction methods, and streamlined node connection and disconnection processes in mapper package
r36
Updated dependencies and go generationUpdated Tailscale dependency to v1.84.3, modified go:generate directives, and added tailscale.com/cmd/viewer tool
r35
Improved ephemeral node handling logicAdded logic to handle ephemeral node deletion during logout and improved node registration and state management in auth and state handling
34 more revisions

Route handling and node management refinedImproved route approval logic, node registration, and integration test handling with more robust route management and error reporting
r33
Simplified batcher error handling logicRemoved complex retry mechanisms, timeouts, and state validation from batcher, streamlining core node connection and work processing logic
r32
Refactored state management and error handlingImproved database operations, policy management, and error handling across multiple components of the headscale system
r31
Enhanced node connection state managementRefactored batcher with robust atomic node operations, improved state validation, error handling, and synchronization mechanisms for node connections and disconnections
r30
Updated dependency versions and routes handlingModified Go module dependencies, updated route management in state and poll logic, and reordered node disconnection and route removal operations
r29
Added .claude directory to gitignoreExpanded .gitignore to include .claude/ directory alongside existing ignored directories and files
r28
Updated batcher tests with MapResponseRefactored test code to use *tailcfg.MapResponse instead of byte slice, removing JSON parsing and zstd decompression logic from test validation functions
r27
Refactor MapResponse Handling LogicRefactored mapper and batcher to directly work with tailcfg.MapResponse instead of marshaling to bytes, removing compression and header management from core logic
r26
Added Docker container resource monitoringImplemented comprehensive Docker container stats collection with memory and CPU tracking, added new CLI flags for resource monitoring and limits
r25
Added fluent MapResponseBuilder for mapperIntroduced a new MapResponseBuilder in mapper package to provide a more flexible and testable way of constructing map responses with chained method calls
r24No changes since last revision
r23
Test expects 6 updates nowUpdated test expectation from 5 to 6 updates for batch change scenario
r22
Scaled back batcher scalability testModified TestBatcherScalability by marking as skippable and reducing test matrix parameters
r21
Multiple code improvements and refactoringRefactored mapper and batcher code, removed unnecessary code, updated type handling, simplified logic in various files including mapper, change tracking, and testing utilities
r20
Removed batcher lock and changegen toolRemoved batcher_lock.go implementation, deleted changegen tool, and simplified batcher test configuration
r19No changes since last revision
r18No changes since last revision
r17
Updated SSH and test configurationModified SSH test scenarios, added error handling in FQDN retrieval, and increased timeout durations for integration tests
r16
Improved traceroute parsing regexUpdated traceroute parsing regex to handle third latency measurement and added safety check for match array length
r15
Modify node change distribution logicUpdated change distribution to allow NodeNewOrUpdate changes to be sent to the originating node
r14
Enhanced SSH policy compilation loggingAdded more detailed trace logging for SSH policy compilation and improved error handling by skipping unresolvable source IPs
r13
Reordered node addition flow sequenceModified node addition process to send initial map first, then mark node connected, and finally notify other nodes about online status
r12
Various code cleanup and minor improvementsImplemented minor code improvements across multiple files, including formatting, linting, code style consistency, and small logic refinements in routing, policy, and testing components
r11
Enhanced route and node change propagationModified SetApprovedRoutes to propagate node and route changes, and updated AddNode to send full map response more safely
r10
Refactored mapper and change notification systemMajor architectural changes to Headscale's mapper and change notification system, introducing a new lock-free batcher, enhanced change tracking, and removing the previous notifier implementation. Adds more granular change propagation mechanisms and improves scalability of node updates.
r9
Refactored change management and notificationsReplaced legacy notification system with new change management approach, introducing a flexible ChangeSet mechanism, batching improvements, and centralized update processing for node and system changes.
r8
Refactored node update and notification systemMajor architectural changes to how node updates are processed, replacing the notifier with a more flexible batcher system, introducing change tracking, and simplifying update propagation across the system
r7
Refactored node notification and batching systemMajor architectural refactoring of node update mechanisms, introducing a new change propagation system with batchers, removing legacy notifier, and improving update processing with lock-free and lock-based implementations
r6
Modified node connection tracking logicUpdated ConnectedMap method to handle nil timestamps for connection status tracking
r5
Headscale refactors change management systemIntroduced a new change management system with improved batcher, mapper, and change tracking mechanisms. Added new change generation tools and restructured node update processes.
r4
Refactored mapper and change detection logicUpdated change detection methods, modified mapper response generation, and renamed some node change detection functions
r3
Refactored mapper and notification systemMajor refactoring of mapper and notification system, introducing a new batching mechanism for node updates and removing complex notification logic
r2
Refactored mapper and notifier componentsSimplified mapper and notifier internals, removing context passing, reducing complexity in node update and notification mechanisms, and consolidating some mapper functionality
r1
Introduced mapper batcher for node updatesRefactored node update handling by introducing a new Batcher in the mapper package, which manages node connection states and asynchronous update processing across multiple components.

message:
mapper: produce map before poll

Before this patch, we would send a message to each "node stream"
that there is an update that needs to be turned into a mapresponse
and sent to a node.

Producing the mapresponse is a "costly" afair which means that while
a node was producing one, it might start blocking and creating full
queues from the poller and all the way up to where updates where sent.

This could cause updates to time out and being dropped as a bad node
going away or spending too time processing would cause all the other
nodes to not get any updates.

In addition, it contributed to "uncontrolled parallel processing" by
potentially doing too many expensive operations at the same time:

Each node stream is essentially a channel, meaning that if you have 30
nodes, we will try to process 30 map requests at the same time. If you
have 8 cpu cores, that will saturate all the cores immediately and cause
a lot of wasted switching between the processing.

Now, all the maps are processed by workers in the mapper, and the number
of workers are controlable. These would now be recommended to be a bit
less than number of CPU cores, allowing us to process them as fast as we
can, and then send them to the poll.

When the poll recieved the map, it is only responsible for taking it and
sending it to the node.

This might not directly improve the performance of Headscale, but it will
likely make the performance a lot more consistent. And I would argue the
design is a lot easier to reason about.

Signed-off-by: Kristoffer Dalby <kristoffer@tailscale.com>
